p: Six years thou shalt sow thy: The Jews began to count the year in September: for then all the fruits were gathered.
own accord of thy harvest thou: Because of the corn that fell out of the ears the previous year.
undressed: Or, which you have separated from yourself, and consecrated to God for the poor.
sabbath of the land shall be: That which the land brings forth in her rest.
Then shalt thou cause the trumpet: In the beginning of the 50 years was the Jubile, so called, because the joyful tidings of liberty were publicly proclaimed by the sound of a cornet.
inhabitants thereof: Which were in bondage.
possession: Because the tribes should neither have their possessions diminished nor confounded.
not oppress one another: By deceit, or otherwise.
years after the jubile thou shalt: If the Jubile to come is near, you would be better to sell cheaply. If it is far off, sell at a higher price.
fruits doth he sell unto thee: And not the full possession of the land.
for ever: It could not be sold for ever, but must return to the family in the Jubile.
grant a redemption for the land: You shall sell it on the condition that it may be redeemed.
count the years of the sale: Deducting money for the years past, and paying for the rest of the years to come.
out: From his hand that bought it.
for ever to him that bought: That is, for ever, read Le 25:23.
suburbs of their cities may not: Where the Levites kept their cattle.
fallen in decay with thee: In Hebrew it is, if his hand shake: meaning if he stretch forth his hand for help as one in misery.
be sold as bondmen: To perpetual servitude.
possession: For they shall not be bought out at the Jubile.
if he be able: If he be able.
years: Which remains yet to the Jubile.
sight: You shall not allow him to treat him severely, if you know it.
